question.text: This Communist, a pioneer of Non-Alignment, was the long time President of Yugoslavia
question.clue: Political opponents of this leader were sent to the prison island of Goli Otok during the Informbiro period.

swap.text: In the US, the hardest ski runs are designated with one or two diamonds of this color.
swap.clue: Gavrilo Princip was a member of a group named for a "hand" of this color, and an overpacked dungeon in Calcutta was known by this color.

question.text: During World War II, Tito fought against this genocidal Croatian political party. Ante Pavelic [PAW-vel-itch] led this party, whose name was appropriated as an anti-Croatian slur during the Yugoslav Wars.
question.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

swap.text: Princip also aligned himself with this secret Serbian military society, which had planted many would-be assassins throughout Sarajevo.
swap.clue: Organized in four or five member committees, its undisputed leader was a man known as "Apis," and its activities were enthusiastically supported for a time by Crown Prince Alexander.

question.text: The Ottomans fought this battle under the command of Murad I against the Serbs under Lazar. While both armies were wiped out, it led to a scarcity of Serbian troops, giving way to Serbian-Ottoman vassalage.
question.clue: Another source congratulates King Tvrtko I for success at this battle, which occurred on St. Vitus Day.

swap.leadin: He kept himself in power and suppressed opposition with the Sigurimi police force.
swap.text: Name this Albanian communist leader, who led Albania through a period of industrialization in the latter half of the twentieth century.
swap.clue: This man was elected Prime Minister of Albania in 1944 and continued to rule until his death in 1985. He ushered in a period of communist rule in Albania that lasted until 1992.

question.text: This 1884 conference organized by the German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck regulated the rules of colonization and attempted to eliminate African autonomy and self-independence.
question.clue: Another key participant here was Gyula Andrassy, who negotiated the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by Austria-Hungary.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the real-life Count Dracula, Vlad the Impaler.
swap.text: While Vlad Dracula is commonly associated with Transylvania, he actually ruled over this region, which was combined with Transylvania and Moldavia to form the modern Romania.
swap.clue: This region was the first one to be ruled by Michael the Brave.

question.leadin: Given details of its twentieth century history, name the eastern European state.
question.text: Todor Zhivkov was the longtime Communist ruler of this country, which was one of the most lockstep allies of the USSR throughout the Cold War.
question.clue: One leader of this nation was ousted after members of the NGO Ecoglasnost were beaten by the police, leading to the one-year term of Petar Mladenov.

swap.leadin: Name these East European Communist leaders.
swap.text: He seized Albania in 1944 and ruled until succeeded by Ramiz Alia in 1981.
swap.clue: A vocal opponent of Mao (+) Zedong's "three worlds" theory, this man was abandoned by his closest ally, China, and successfully imposed state atheism despite his country's majority Muslim population.

question.text: The Hungarian Revolution was partially put down by Josip Jelacic ("YO-seep YAY-la-cheech"), a military leader of this ethnicity. Nationalists of this ethnicity formed the Ustase ("OO-stah-sheh") during World War II.
question.clue: People of this nationality received very little power over taxation in a dissatisfying agreement called the Nagodba, which did, however, allow them to elect their sabor.

swap.leadin: Name some instances of history and soccer coming together.
swap.text: This country's war of independence from Yugoslavia and various other Serb influences began at a 1990 soccer match between Red Star Belgrade and the "Dinamo" team from this country's capital.
swap.clue: This country was merged with Slavonia in 1868, though Rijeka ] remained separate.

question.leadin: Besides Germany, this country contributed the most troops to the fascist invasion of the USSR.
question.text: Name this country, which lost Bessarabia and North Bukovina in the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and then regained those territories in Operation Barbarossa. This country's Conducator overthrew its king Carol II.
question.clue: Though briefly restored by King Michael's Coup, this country's monarchy was abolished and replaced by the Iron Guard in 1940.

swap.text: Benedetto Cotrugli, an economist from this city, described an early version of double-entry bookkeeping. This city became a major maritime republic after being transferred from Venice to Hungary in the Treaty of Zadar.
swap.clue: The nobles of this city elected its leaders to a position known as either Rector or knez ("k'nez").

question.leadin: The Treaty of San Stefano prompted Abdyl Frasheri to lead the League of Prizren in resistance against the partition of lands inhabited by this ethnic group.
question.text: Name these people whose first prime minister Ismail Qemali waved the flag from the Assembly of Vlore ("VLAW-ruh") after declaring independence in 1912.
question.clue: People of this ethnicity were the target of the Racak Massacre, whose perpetrators claimed to be targeting a paramilitary group led by Hashim Thaci .

swap.leadin: Name the following 20th century eastern European leaders.
swap.text: This patron of Nicolae Ceausescu was the Communist leader of Romania from 1948 to 1965. Domestically, he emphasized the manufacturing of consumer goods, while he sought to improve foreign relations with both the West and China.
swap.clue: Together with Petru Groza, this Romanian leader reportedly held King Michael at gunpoint to convince him to abdicate. After becoming prime minister in 1952, he forged alliances with China and other non-communist states, before being succeeded as party leader by Nicolae Ceausescu ("chow-SHES-koo").

question.text: Enver Hoxha, Ramiz Alia, Ed Cohn, and other leaders of Communist Albania stayed in power thanks to this secret police force that oppressed those whose ideology was deemed revisionist; it was at least nominally abolished in 1991.

swap.text: The Great Power's ineffectual original choice for King of Albania, William of Wied ("VEED"), ruled from this city until the Congress of Lushnje ("LUSH-nyuh"). Lodewijk ("loh-deh-WIKE") Thomson died defending this city from Haxhi Qamili's ("HAH-jee CHYAH-muh-lee's") pro-Ottoman peasant revolt.
swap.clue: Under Ottoman rule this city was a major market town in the Vilayet of Scutari, and in 1914 it became the capital of a kingdom led at the time by Prince William of Wied.

question.text: Tuđman launched Operation Storm and obliterated the forces of Serbian Krajina after agreeing to lend this leader military aid via the Split Agreement. With Tuđman and Slobodon Milosevic, this first President of Bosnia and Herzegovina signed the 1995 Dayton Accords.

swap.leadin: This time lasted from 1948 to 1954 and was named for the organization controlled by Stalin which Yugoslavia did not wish to join.
swap.text: Identify this period, during which Yugoslavia's refusal to join the Warsaw Pact led to the constant threat of Soviets deposing the Yugoslavian leadership.
swap.clue: This period during which over 100 citizens were killed at the Goli Otok ("GOH-lee OH-toke") prison camp. The Belgrade declaration ended this seven-year period with a rapprochement between the Soviet Union and another nation.
